subject: literature
passage: I had been at Harwood scarcely a fortnight before Mr. Pell began to call upon us with a regularity that the whole parish remarked. My aunt, who had buried two husbands and had no intention of acquiring a nephew-in-law she disliked, received him in the front parlor with a courtesy so exact that it amounted to a rebuke. It had been settled, by an understanding never once spoken aloud between my aunt and ______, that his attentions were to be met with civility and returned with nothing warmer; and so, each Thursday, I poured his tea, admired his opinions of the weather, and wished him safely home.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The blank is part of the compound object of the preposition "between" ("between my aunt and ___"). The object of a preposition must be an object pronoun, so the narrator refers to herself as "me." A quick test is to remove "my aunt and": "between ... me" is correct, not "between ... I."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "I" is a subject pronoun, but the blank is the object of the preposition "between."
explanation.B: Correct. "Me" is the object pronoun needed after the preposition "between."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Mine" is a possessive pronoun meaning "belonging to me," which makes no sense as one of the two people sharing the understanding.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Myself" is reflexive and is used only when "I" is the subject of the same clause; here the subject is "It," so the object form "me" is needed.
